tasks.short: Review a clinical protocol for submission data

steps.what: Submit the protocol and the endpoint list
List the data a submission must collect

loop.input: protocol sections and the submission data checklist
loop.output: data items each citing a section id
loop.check: Each item names a section id that exists in the protocol
loop.stop: One pass, then leave the item blank if no section matches
loop.why_not_simpler: Protocol prose does not follow one table, so a fixed merge cannot see a renamed section

steps.what: Judge which gaps would block a submission
Revise the protocol where data are missing
Sign this protocol review version
File only the signed protocol review

tasks.design: The project lead files the protocol, the endpoint list and the submission type on a {PROJECT} record. A bounded pass over the checklist in {DOCS} lists only data items that cite a protocol section. The specialist signs one review version, and only that version is stored.
tasks.previous_blocker: Protocols arrived as long documents with different headings, so a checklist could not tell a missing endpoint from a renamed section.
tasks.enabler_now: The project record can carry a protocol section id next to each endpoint, which a draft can check.
tasks.still_hard: Whether a missing data item would actually block a submission is still a scientific and regulatory call.
tasks.human_edge: The specialist decides which gaps matter for the submission and which are wording only.

ambition.what: Review the protocol again when the endpoint list changes, not only before the first submission

tasks.altitude: Less time building the checklist, the same duty to refuse a review that cites a section the protocol does not have. The filed version is the one the specialist signed.

reach.task: Revise the protocol section marked blank
reach.learn: Which data items are signed as sufficient and which are still open

evidence.claim: In a mid-size firm this review is a document read. The checklist is the repeatable part; the gap call is not.
Digest [S27] says a consultancy partly repaid a public report that cited sources that did not exist, so a protocol comment must not invent a data requirement.
Clinical protocols often contain health details. The draft stays in the document store and is not sent outside the review.

assumptions: Focal role is the regulatory affairs specialist. The task ends when the signed review version is filed. Running the study is out of scope.

Input contract: protocol id, section id, endpoint name, submission type, market, project id. Producer is the project lead. If a section id is missing, that item stays blank and is not guessed from the title.
Use the document store's own checklist and approval flow before custom code. The meeting share in the prior is small; this review stays on the document, not in a standing meeting.
Protocol text is not copied into a model prompt that leaves the firm. Health details stay in the document store.
unknowns: Whether these protocols identify patients or only study procedures.
Who may sign a review when the specialist is absent.
Which submission types have an agreed data checklist.
research_questions: What share of protocol reviews find an endpoint with no section id?
How often does the signed review differ from the first gap list?

already_counted.description: Specialist edits data items the checklist matched weakly
Gap judgement stays in the review and is not deducted again

incremental.description: Extend the data checklist when a new submission type appears
Project leads resubmit endpoints that have no section id

approvals.approved_version: protocol review version signed in this review
the same signed protocol review version

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes most protocols still arrive as unstructured files, so the checklist rarely matches and the specialist reads as today. The high case assumes section ids exist but every gap decision and the signature stay manual. The study itself is not treated as saved.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Take part in an internal or external audit

steps.what: Issue the internal audits plan and sample list
Assemble the records the plan names
Examine the sample and ask questions
Answer the auditor from those records
Draft the response from the audit notes

loop.input: finding ids on the audit notes and the response template
loop.output: response that cites finding ids only
loop.check: Every finding id in the draft is on the audit notes
loop.stop: One draft, then drop any finding that was not recorded
loop.why_not_simpler: The meaning of a finding is not a fixed sentence

steps.what: Sign this audit response version
File only the signed audit response

tasks.design: The quality reviewer puts the audit plan and the sample list on a {WORKFLOW} form. The specialist assembles those records in {DOCS} before the room. A bounded note drafts the response from recorded findings only, and only the signed response is filed.
tasks.previous_blocker: The sample list lived in mail and the findings lived in notes, so a response could not show which record it relied on.
tasks.enabler_now: The plan can name a record id for each sample, and the room notes can name a finding id.
tasks.still_hard: Answering the auditor, and deciding what a finding means, stays in the room with the specialist.
tasks.human_edge: The specialist chooses what to say in the room and what the written response may claim.
tasks.altitude: The pack is ready before the audit. The specialist still attends, still answers, and can refuse a response that cites a finding nobody recorded.

reach.task: Close a corrective action the specialist signed
reach.learn: Which findings are accepted in the signed response and which are still open

evidence.claim: Audit time in a mid-size firm is the sample and the room. Filing the response is the smaller part, and the room does not become a form.
Digest [S27] says a consultancy partly repaid a public report that cited sources that did not exist, so an audit response must not invent a finding or a rule.

assumptions: Focal role is the regulatory affairs specialist. The task runs from the audit plan to a signed response, or to a stopped draft. It does not include the later corrective project.

Input contract: audit id, sample record id, finding id, question text, internal or external flag. Producer of the plan is the quality reviewer. An external questioner is the agency reviewer. A sample with no record id is fetched by hand and marked manual.
The workflow shape in the prior is high. That fits the pack and the filing, not the room. Native document links are configured before a new audit tool. This design does not score staff.
unknowns: Whether internal audits use the quality reviewer in the chair the agency reviewer uses externally.
Which record stores are in the sample.
Who may sign a response when the specialist is absent.
research_questions: What share of audit hours is spent in the room rather than assembling the pack?
How often does a response cite a finding that was not on the note list?

already_counted.description: Specialist corrects a draft that cites a weak finding
Time in the audit room stays with the specialist

incremental.description: Keep the response template aligned with new finding types
Quality reviewers fix sample rows that have no record id

approvals.approved_version: audit response version signed for this audit id
the same signed audit response version

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes sample lists stay free text, so the pack is still built by hand and the draft rarely fires. The high case assumes record ids are clean but the room, the answers and the signature stay manual. No finding is closed by the filing step.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Keep the regulatory document register current

steps.what: Submit the document identity and version
Match the record fields to the file
Decide which version is current
Store the signed regulatory documentation version
Clear duplicate or incomplete records

tasks.design: Project leads submit document id, product id, market, version and effective date on a {WORKFLOW} form. A field check in {DOCS} rejects a row that does not match the file. The specialist signs which version is current, and only that version stays visible.
tasks.previous_blocker: The same document existed as a file, a mail copy and a row, and nothing recorded which version was current.
tasks.enabler_now: The file and the register can share one document id and one version, so a mismatch is a field check rather than a reread.
tasks.still_hard: Deciding which version is current, and retiring another, is still the specialist's call when two copies both look valid.
tasks.human_edge: The specialist chooses the current version and stops a row that would hide the wrong file.

ambition.what: Mark a document current in the week it is approved, not in a monthly tidy-up

tasks.altitude: The specialist leaves matching rows alone and keeps the queue of conflicts and retirements. A machine cannot make a version current without that signature.

reach.task: Use the current document in the submission pack
reach.learn: Which version is signed as current and which version was retired

evidence.claim: Digest [S14] says Veeva RIM tracks registrations and publishes submissions. That supports a register of versions. It does not decide which version is current.
The digest's deterministic-first section treats records and monitoring as a records app on operational data, with a person still accountable for the status.
Digest [S27] says a consultancy partly repaid a public report that cited sources that did not exist, so a register row must not invent an approval the file does not show.

assumptions: Focal role is the regulatory affairs specialist. The task is the register of regulatory documents, not the scientific writing inside them.

Input contract: document id, product id, market, version, effective date, owner, status. Producer is the project lead. A row with no document id or no version is rejected and not completed by guesswork. If the file header lacks those fields, the specialist types them once and marks the row manual.
Configure the existing register's fields and its own approval step before building a second store. A spreadsheet is only the fallback when the register cannot hold a version.
unknowns: Whether one register is already the source of current versions.
Who may retire a version when the specialist is absent.
Which markets use a different document id for the same file.
research_questions: What share of documents have two versions marked current?
How many new rows arrive in a typical week without a version?

already_counted.description: Specialist reviews rows the field check flagged
The current-version decision stays with the specialist
Duplicate cleanup stays with the specialist

incremental.description: Add a register field when a new market needs a different status
Project leads correct rows the form rejects

approvals.approved_version: current-version decision for this document id

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes many files have no document id, so the field check rejects them and the specialist still files by hand. The high case assumes ids match but every current-version decision and every conflict stays with the specialist. Reading the scientific content is not treated as saved.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Recommend procedure changes after a rule change

steps.what: Open the procedure index for this market
Decide which procedures must change
Draft the recommendation from that decision

loop.input: procedure ids marked change and the rule note text
loop.output: recommendation that names those ids and quotes the note
loop.check: Every procedure id is on the change decision and every quote is in the rule note
loop.stop: One draft; if the decision is no change, write that line only and stop
loop.why_not_simpler: Whether a sentence of the rule requires a change is not a lookup

steps.what: Comment on whether the floor can comply
Sign the recommendation staff would follow
Publish only the signed change note

tasks.design: A {WORKFLOW} index lists procedure id, product and market. The specialist decides which procedures a rule note affects. A bounded note in {DOCS} drafts the recommendation from that decision and the rule text, and only the signed note is published.
tasks.previous_blocker: Rule notes and procedure lists were separate documents, so a draft could not show which procedure a sentence was about.
tasks.enabler_now: The index can key a procedure id to a product and a market, and the rule note can be stored as text with its own document id.
tasks.still_hard: Whether a rule note requires a procedure change at all is a judgement, and the applicable rule is whatever the specialist confirms.
tasks.human_edge: The specialist decides which procedures must change and signs the note staff will be asked to follow.

ambition.what: Issue the recommendation when the rule note arrives, not only at the yearly procedure review

tasks.altitude: The specialist spends the week on the change-or-not call. A recommendation staff must follow exists only as the signed note, and a machine publishes nothing else.

reach.task: Assign an owner only to a procedure the note marks for change
reach.learn: Which procedures are in the signed note and which were marked no change

evidence.claim: The digest's deterministic-first section groups procedure drafts as a bounded loop over approved sources, with a named person signing.
Digest [S27] says a consultancy partly repaid a public report that cited sources that did not exist, so the note must not invent an instrument or a procedure id.
Which rule applies is confirmed by the specialist for the product and the market. This task does not name an instrument.

assumptions: Focal role is the regulatory affairs specialist. The task ends at the signed recommendation. Rewriting the procedure text is a separate task.

Input contract: rule document id, rule text, procedure id, product id, market, change or no-change. Producer of the procedure index is the quality system owner via the quality reviewer. If the rule text has no document id, the draft is empty and the specialist writes the note by hand.
Use the document store's template and approval flow before custom code. The note does not change a procedure until this signature, and the signature is void if the rule text changes.
unknowns: Whether a no-change decision must be filed or can stay on the index.
Who may sign when the specialist is absent.
research_questions: What share of rule notes end as no change?
How often does the signed note name a procedure that is not on the index?

already_counted.description: The change-or-not decision stays with the specialist
Specialist edits the draft before signing

incremental.description: Update the procedure index when a procedure is split or renamed
Quality reviewers return comments on procedures they cannot run

approvals.approved_version: procedure recommendation version signed in this review
the same signed procedure recommendation version

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes rule notes stay unfiled prose, so the draft does not run and the specialist still compares by hand. The high case assumes the index is clean but every change-or-not call and every signature stays manual. The later procedure rewrite is not treated as saved.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The specialist stops retyping protocol checklists and document rows, and keeps the week for gap decisions, audit rooms and procedure calls.
reach: Quality reviewers receive the signed audit response and the current document status, instead of a folder of drafts.
Project leads receive the protocol gaps and the signed procedure recommendation.
skills_to_grow: Write a submission data need as a checklist field tied to a protocol section.
Mark one document version as current and retire the previous version.
Separate a procedure recommendation from the later rewrite of the procedure itself.
role.ambitious_version: Protocol reviews, audit responses and procedure recommendations exist only as a signed version, and the register shows that version alone.
